conceptDrafts.logline: When a drought drops the reservoir and exposes a car with a body inside, a small-town claims adjuster realizes the insurance file she closed twenty years ago — the one that paid for her house — was the cover story, and every adult she loves helped write it.

concept.summary: A drought exposes a submerged car with a body in Lake Verity, and the 1999 drowning-accident file that claims adjuster Nora Pell closed as her first case reopens. The payout from that file bought her mother's house. The victim turns out to be her mother's first husband — a man the town believed ran off. Nora investigates her own family and her own signature, while her mother, her stepfather (the town's retired pharmacist), and her childhood best friend (now the county detective assigned to the case) each protect a different piece of what happened. Every reveal re-prices a relationship; the mystery IS the family.

characters.name: Nora Pell
characters.backstory: Closed the drowning file at 24 as her first solo case; the payout cleared her mother's mortgage. Built a careful life on a signature she never questioned.
characters.motivations: Establish what she actually signed and who arranged for her to sign it.
characters.flaws: Treats documentation as truth; would rather amend a record than have a conversation.
characters.need: To learn who she is when the paper is wrong.
characters.arc: From adjuster to claimant against her own family.

relationships.description: her mother — the beneficiary of the file Nora signed
her stepfather — married her mother two years after the 'accident'
childhood best friend — now the detective on the reopened case

characters.name: Marion Pell
characters.backstory: Widow of the man in the reservoir — though the town believed he ran off, and she let them. Remarried the pharmacist who was kindest during the search.
characters.motivations: Keep her daughter from learning which parts of the story were built for her.
characters.flaws: Protects people by editing their reality; calls it kindness.
characters.need: To be known by her daughter and survive it.
characters.arc: From curator of the story to its confessor.

relationships.description: her daughter — protected by the lie, paid by the claim
second husband — the man who helped the story hold
her daughter's friend — the child who saw the car leave

characters.name: Gil Harmon
characters.backstory: The town pharmacist for forty years; filled every prescription and knew every dose in the county, including the one in the dead man's blood.
characters.motivations: Die respected; keep Marion's family intact the way he helped rebuild it.
characters.flaws: Believes a good outcome retroactively justifies its chemistry.
characters.need: To say out loud what the kindness cost.
characters.arc: From beloved elder to the season's quietest confession.

relationships.description: his wife — he married the widow he helped make
stepdaughter — the adjuster whose signature closed his handiwork

characters.name: Detective Dess Okafor
characters.backstory: Nora's best friend since fourth grade; was eleven when she saw a car towed up the old boat ramp at night and was told she dreamed it. Now assigned to the body.
characters.motivations: Work the case straight in a town that raised her crooked.
characters.flaws: Recuses herself from nothing; believes friendship and procedure can both survive this.
characters.need: To accept the case ends her version of home.
characters.arc: From hometown cop to the one who reads Nora her rights, or doesn't.

relationships.description: best friend — and now the adjuster of record is her person of interest
the woman who told an eleven-year-old she was dreaming
